title: Cold start: why 'just add content-based' does not work
summary: Lecture 4 (content-based) + Lecture 1: the cold-start fix people reach for first and the reason it underdelivers.
angle: Content-based features solve item cold start only where the catalog metadata is as discriminative as behaviour - which is almost never.

title: Offline NDCG went up, CTR went down: three reasons
summary: Lecture 3 (metrics): the standard offline/online divergence modes - position bias in the logs, popularity leakage, and a target that is not the business one.
angle: Ranking metrics on logged data measure how well you reproduce the old policy, not how good the new one is.

title: Two-tower retrieval: what actually eats the latency budget
summary: Lecture 7 (highload service): where the p99 goes in a real retrieval path - ANN, feature fetch, and the network hops nobody counts.
angle: The model is rarely the bottleneck; feature fetching and fan-out are.

title: Sequential models: when SASRec is worth it and when it is not
summary: Lecture 5: the session-length and catalog-churn conditions under which sequence models beat matrix factorization.
angle: Sequence models pay off with long, ordered sessions and a fast-churning catalog - otherwise you buy latency for nothing.

title: Popularity bias quietly kills the long tail
summary: How feedback loops concentrate exposure, and the standard countermeasures with their costs.
angle: Most 'diversity' fixes trade measurable CTR for unmeasured retention, which is why they get rolled back.

title: Reading the X (Twitter) algorithm sources
summary: Open-sourced ranking stack in recSys_course/x-algorithm - the candidate sourcing and heavy-ranker split.
angle: The interesting part is not the model - it is how aggressively they prune before ranking.

title: Netflix deep-learning case study, for a 10-engineer team
summary: Netflix DL for recommenders deck - which pieces survive without their infrastructure.
angle: Most of the Netflix stack is an answer to their scale; the transferable part is the offline/online evaluation discipline.

title: Automating my own LinkedIn with GitHub Actions and an LLM
summary: This repository: harvest, draft, critic pass, Telegram approval, LinkedIn Posts API.
angle: The interesting engineering problem was not generation - it was the approval loop and keeping the voice from drifting.

title: Speculative decoding: numbers from my own experiment
summary: From speculative_decoding_ma - measured speedup vs acceptance rate.
angle: Speculative decoding gives you throughput only when the draft model is cheap AND well aligned; one without the other is a loss.

title: The metrics I stopped showing stakeholders
summary: Which recsys metrics create bad decisions in review meetings and what replaced them.
angle: Reporting offline ranking metrics to non-ML stakeholders trains them to ask for the wrong things.
